Subject: DPA draft + questions on Dedicated vs Private language

Hi Diego / Marissa,

Thanks for the updated DPA. A few quick clarifications from our side before we loop in procurement:

- Subprocessors: we need the full list of subprocessors that will touch EU customer data for Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) vs the Private/VPC option. Can you confirm whether the same infra partners (edge cache, metrics) are considered subprocessors when a customer opts for Private?
- Transfers: BlueSky requires either SCCs or an alternative adequacy route for any cross-border transfers. Our legal team is pushing for explicit SCC language and a data flow diagram.
- Execution: will this go via DocuSign? We prefer DocuSign for the audit trail.

I've attached our standard procurement checklist and marked the DPA items we particularly care about (liability cap, audit rights, and subprocessors).

Appreciate a short call if helpful — lot of stakeholders on our end.

Best,
Anna

Subject: Re: DPA draft + questions on Dedicated vs Private language

Anna — thanks. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) Subprocessors: we maintain a single inventory (RI-Subprocessor-Inventory-20261130.csv attached). For Dedicated (reserved capacity) we surface a subset (infra partners that run on the shared control plane) and for Private/VPC we list only agents that will have any access to telemetry or managed services. Practically: some observability providers are not engaged in Private when the customer elects fully on-prem. We will add a clear table in the DPA that maps deployment mode -> subprocessors engaged.

2) Transfers & SCCs: Redwood proposes SCC incorporation by reference plus a migration clause — if adequacy law changes we will swap in appropriate safeguards. We also propose an exhibit with a simple data flow diagram and the contractual assurances for how we treat KV cache and prefixes in Dedicated vs Private.

3) Execution: yes, DocuSign. We can prepare an envelope and mark the DPA as the primary exhibit.

Next steps: Marissa will circulate a tracked-redline with the mapping table; Rishi will review the SCC language and the proposed exhibit; Soojin will confirm which observability partners are excluded for fully private/on-prem installs. Can we aim to have a DocuSign envelope ready by EOD Thursday?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call if BlueSky prefers.

— Diego

Reviewed Section 7.2 and the proposed exhibit. Two items to flag for BlueSky:

1) SCCs by reference are fine, but recommend adding explicit wording that subprocessor engagements that result in cross-border transfers will be covered under the same SCC regime. This closes a gap where a subprocessor contract could rely on a different transfer mechanism.

2) For Private/on-prem installs, we should add an explicit statement: "No Redwood-managed telemetry will be routed to third-party processors unless the customer elects managed monitoring in writing." That gives BlueSky a clear assurance.

I've added suggested one-line text for both and attached a clean copy of the paragraph to include in the tracked doc.

Rishi
